scope: Phase-two fourth batch: application-owned runtime execution, registered controls/options/time settings and native-lifetime-bearing debug targets. SDK unchanged.
status: Functional checks passed. The 11-group paired Release comparison and final same-program control meet the unchanged 3% timing limits; two earlier noisy controls and an invalid extended run are retained. Unmeasured counters remain open. Phase two is in progress and completed_phase stays one.
implemented: ExecutionCommands owns Debugger, its advancement and copied runtime state. Remaining breakpoint views retain only a const inspection pointer; UI-native mutation entry points were removed.

Status bar, application/Schematic shortcuts, debug controls, fullscreen keys and startup playback dispatch registered runtime commands. Play/Pause resolves the configured Play/Pause providers through the same registry.

Play/Pause/Reset, frame/debug stepping, Leave Behavior, Execute Scripts, Trace, debug limits/options/locks and time settings reuse existing core behavior. Reset keeps its previous topology refresh and Dirty behavior without adding an undo step.

runtime.state, runtime.time and runtime.log are read-only value projections usable while file work owns native access. Runtime commands and automatic advancement refuse native work during file tasks or an open edit.

Version-five public C descriptors add finite real values and named execution states. Numeric settings are checked before native writes, including NaN/infinity/range validation, integer overflow and invalid time ranges.

Current debug objects and log targets use ObjectRef, backed by SDK object lifetimes. Existing debug locks keep references and only derive native IDs at use. Same-ID replacements cannot inherit those records.
A monotonic native failure count lets the application report guarded runtime failures as failed commands while preserving the engine's existing pause/reset behavior.
Native budget behavior is unchanged; no process isolation, forced native interruption, SDK alteration or GPU transfer change is included.

checks.build: macos-arm64 Release production editor, core/native tests, native UI test executable and independent modules built successfully.

module_ui_inventory.note: Unselected Test Engine cases are not counted as passed.

regressions: Actual built-in status buttons invoke an independently compiled Play provider, then preserve frame limit, pause, step and reset behavior.
Rebound Trace shortcut replaces its default accelerator in the Schematic. Inside Frames enables Trace; the real Time Settings form submits finite numeric values through registered commands.
Malformed booleans, integer overflow, nonfinite/overflowing FPS, invalid time bounds and a mixed valid/invalid Script batch fail before native mutation.
Read-only runtime/time/log data remains available during native exclusion; mutations, advancement, open-edit access and wrong-thread commands are refused.
Deferred real values survive caller mutation; closing a command view cancels queued runtime work.
A guarded native PreProcess exception reports command failure. Existing ScriptDebugger and full-frame time-budget regressions pass.
Debug lock expiry, queued stale lock requests, document replacement and log target deletion with same-ID reuse retain the original object lifetimes.
Independent C/C++ header consumers pass without STL/SDK/SDL headers. Complete file-byte compatibility and generated NMO direct-open regressions pass.

sdk.note: --sdk-change permits the already authorized identity changes present in both programs. No new SDK source change or all-green SDK test run is claimed.

control_diagnosis.symptom: Both identical programs slowed across sequential groups; current MAD 3.854674%, reference MAD 3.192272%, above the unchanged 3% limit.
observations: Both program hashes and launch/CPU policies match; all five stable transfer/resource counters remain zero.
Read-only system inspection found an unrelated watchpoint process near one CPU core, WindowServer around 40% and Spotlight processes around 20% each.
pmset reported no recorded thermal or performance warning.
control_diagnosis.interpretation: The same-program measurement is nonstationary. External load is a plausible contributor, not a proven single cause; no source fix or threshold change was made.
control_diagnosis.followup: A second unchanged control still exceeded the 3% MAD limit. An attempted 21-group extension hit the native test watchdog. The final original 11-group control passed (+0.255625%, MAD 1.016297%/0.901419%); earlier failures remain retained and show that the host was not uniformly quiet. No threshold, source or harness change was made.

invalid_extended_run.reason: The reference native UI test exceeded the existing 60-second Test Engine watchdog and exited unsuccessfully; its GPU assertions passed, but the failed run cannot be accepted. The candidate did not produce a complete capture.
invalid_extended_run.followup: Returned to the original 11-group protocol. No test watchdog or performance limit was relaxed.

performance.interpretation: The recorded paired comparison changed +0.687868% (current MAD 0.553533%, reference 0.306359%) and the final identical-program control changed +0.255625% (MAD 1.016297%/0.901419%). Both meet the 3% limits for this macOS Metal scene. Earlier controls failed under changing host load; these measurements do not establish universal frame-time stability or any unmeasured counter.

remaining: Phase two still contains webpage/print ownership and document replacement failure combinations.
Full breakpoint/initial-condition editing and complex debugger/diagnostic views remain with their planned view migration. The const legacy inspection path is explicit.
A permanently stuck native plugin still cannot be forcibly interrupted. Process isolation remains a separate change and must retain the embedded viewport.
15 original-sample suites are absent and skipped. Native desktop/fullscreen acceptance and Windows/Linux execution remain separate.
GPU-only timestamps, application allocation counts, preserve-copy/pass/submit counts, native capability queries and retain/release are not measured by this harness.
